title: Do antidepressants increase the risk of mania and bipolar disorder in people with depression? A retrospective electronic case register cohort study
authors: Patel R, Reiss P, Shetty H, Broadbent M, Stewart R, McGuire P, et al.
followUp: diagnoses April 2006 to March 2013, censored at 31 March 2014
population: Adults with unipolar depression in secondary mental healthcare at South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
funder: RP is supported by a UK Medical Research Council Clinical Research Training Fellowship (MR/K002813/1). HS, MB, RS and MT are funded by the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre at South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust and King's College London, which also supports the CRIS data resource.
authorConflicts: The CRIS team (HS, MB, RS) have received research funding from Roche, Pfizer, J&J and Lundbeck; PM from Janssen, Sunovion, GW and Roche; MT personal fees from Bristol-Myers Squibb and Otsuka outside the work.
result: Incidence of mania or bipolar disorder 10.9 per 1000 person-years overall, 12.3 at ages 26 to 35, and 13.1 to 19.1 per 1000 person-years after prior antidepressant treatment; adjusted hazard ratio for SSRIs 1.34 (95% CI 1.18 to 1.52), venlafaxine 1.35 (1.07 to 1.70). Observational; a causal link cannot be inferred.
